newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals drift in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals drift in subdued trade.

text.p: Gold meandered in a narrow price range on Thursday after starting the day on a weaker note, while the platinum and palladium drifted lower.
"Things are quite dead," a bullion dealer said. "It looked for a while like gold was testing $342 and might go lower, but it seems to be holding well at these levels."
Gold was fixed at $342.20 an ounce, compared to $341.80 in the morning.
Bullion had started the weaker compared to Wednesday's close of $343.80/344.30 after the dollar firmed sharply against the yen in Asian trading hours.
The surge brought out heavy bullion selling in the Far East as investors took advantage of higher domestic prices.
Silver was also very quiet and last indicated down just a cent at $4.75/4.77.
Platinum and palladium, meanwhile, ticked lower after some lending entered the market early in the day.
"People are trying to stay out the PGMs (platinum group metals) as much as possible, but there has been a little turnover today," a dealer said.
Both metals were vulnerable to extreme volatility in the case of a glitch in Russia opening its export campaign to Japan next month, dealers said.
Russia, which provides over 60 percent of the world's palladium and around 25 percent of its platinum, has been out of the market since December due to administrative problems.
"There is still volatility in the market. Russia has said it will export (to Japan) as soon as possible but that could still be the very end of June," a dealer said.
Platinum was quoted at $439.00/$444.00, down $16 from Wednesday's close.
